transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 09:24 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Marino (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (Redwood CSM); Karen Lu (Pioneer RL, Head MLOps), Marco Diaz (CTO), Sophie Tan (Procurement), Eli Grant (Infra), Tanya Rivera (Product), Vendor Booth (intern)
Recording note: auto-generated; some proper nouns may be off.

Auto-summary (auto):
Redwood and Pioneer Retail Labs reviewed renewal timings and a multi-region uplift playbook. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted with an eye on UK region capacity and private VPC constraints. Action items agreed: Redwood to provide updated quote, SE to run UK benchmarks, customer to confirm procurement timeline.

Topics: renewal timeline, regional onboarding (UK), Dedicated capacity vs. burst, VPC/private deployment constraints, SOC2 + compliance artifacts, PO timing.

Action items (in call): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the renewal playbook and the regional uplift ask.
[00:18] Karen: Hi Alex, Karen here. We've got Marco, Sophie and Eli on — thanks.
[00:28] Marco: Morning.
[00:31] Sophie: Hi all.
[00:33] Priya: Hi team, Priya Shah, solutions engineer. I'll handle the technical checklist and benchmark plan.
[00:40] Alex: Cool. Quick context — you mentioned wanting to add UK region in Q2 and bump capacity by roughly 2.5x, and also discuss the contract term. Is that still accurate?
[01:05] Karen: Yep that's the ask. We're seeing more traffic from UK and EU customers; latency matters for checkout micro interactions. We'd rather not multi-cloud host ourselves.
[01:19] Marco: To add, we need predictable tail latency for the widget at 99th pct — ideally <200ms across the board. Cost matters but predictable performance is the gating factor.
[01:33] Priya: Understood. We've got two obvious levers: Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and Private (VPC) deployment if you need data residency and tighter networking. Hosting gives fastest time-to-value but has slightly less predictable tail latency for very spiky workloads.
[01:55] Sophie: When you say Private, do you mean we get a customer-managed control plane or is that fully Redwood-managed?
[02:09] Alex: Private = customer-controlled network (VPC peering or PrivateLink) and optional on-prem packages. Control plane still runs with Redwood for orchestration unless you choose the fully air-gapped on-prem option. We can share the exact network diagram.
[02:30] Eli: If we go VPC, we need egress IPs, and we need to run traffic through our KMS. Does Redwood support external KMS?
[02:46] Priya: Yes — we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers and can bring-your-own keys. There was a small hiccup last quarter with one customer's key rotation flow but we've already patched that behavior in the runtime.
[03:05] Marco: Good to hear. Also, can Dedicated be configured to autoscale burst during flash sales? We don't want cold starts in the holiday spikes.
[03:18] Priya: Dedicated supports burst policies and configurable autoscaling windows. The tradeoff is committed cost vs on-demand overage. For your pattern (2.5x baseline, spiky bursts), we often recommend a smaller Dedicated base and a burst buffer to avoid over-committing monthly.
[03:41] Alex: We'll put those options in the quote — base Dedicated + burst pool + hosted fallback for overflow.
[03:50] Karen: What's the expected latency delta between Dedicated and Hosted?
[03:56] Priya: In our benchmarks, Dedicated with pinned kernels and local NVMe for KV cache runs ~15–30ms better median and significantly less variance at tail for 2k token sequences versus multi-tenant hosted. But heavy quantized models can narrow that gap. I can attach the benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:21] Marco: And for UK region specifically — do you have capacity there now?
[04:27] Alex: We have hosted endpoints in UK region, Dedicated pools can be provisioned but lead time depends on GPU availability — typically 2–4 weeks for standard reserved capacity, sometimes longer for specific hardware.
[04:45] Eli: That's tight. We need to go live mid-April ideally. Is 2–4 weeks realistic?
[04:52] Priya: If you accept a short pilot on hosted UK edges we can get you live in days, while the Dedicated pool is being provisioned. That is a common path.
[05:04] Sophie: Procurement question — if we start with hosted and then pop into Dedicated, will there be a change order or a break in billing?
[05:12] Alex: No break in API compatibility. Billing will transition — we will roll expected credits/commitments into the new contract. We'll outline the seat-level and token-level math in the quote.
[05:25] Tanya: One question on observability — can we get request traces and token-cost breakdown per route? Our finance team needs per-feature cost attribution.
[05:35] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per route, plus tracing hooks. We can add per-route dashboards in the onboarding playbook.
[05:47] Marco: Security: we need SOC2 and potentially an ISO attestation. Any blockers there?
[05:53] Alex: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO in progress; we'll share the latest reports and the security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security/PRL-pack).
[06:06] Karen: Great. One more: encryption in transit AND at rest with customer-managed keys — confirmed?
[06:12] Priya: Confirmed. Also audit logs are available for model invocations if you need long retention — that's an add-on.
[06:24] Marco: Okay. Let's talk numbers. Sophie can you outline your procurement constraints?
[06:30] Sophie: We have to sign before end of April to hit budget cycle. Preferred term is 12–24 months; we can consider multi-year for better rates. Also need a PO and legal redlines no later than April 15.
[06:46] Alex: Noted. We'll aim to get a formal quote to you by next Wednesday (Mar 24).
[06:52] Karen: On capacity, we're estimating 600k tokens/day now with a projected ramp to 1.5M in six weeks; most requests are short (200–400 tokens) but checkout flows are sensitive.
[07:07] Priya: That pattern is helpful. For that volume Dedicated base + hosted burst looks cost-effective. Also, prefix/KV caching will reduce token compute for repeat flows — we'll recommend cache TTLs and suggestion for caching keys.
[07:26] Marco: Quick aside — does your runtime support LLM quantization variants? We are evaluating 8-bit and 4-bit options for cost optimization.
[07:35] Priya: Yes, we support a set of quantized model variants; the runtime picks kernels accordingly. For checkout scenarios where quality is important, we usually recommend 8-bit. 4-bit is great for embeddings or lower-critical content.
[07:50] Eli: Any known regressions with 4-bit on the ops stack?
[07:54] Priya: There can be degredation (sic) on some tight prompt sets; we recommend a short eval on your prompts — we can run that during the benchmark.
[08:05] Alex: Okay, so plan: SE runs prompt-anchored evals in UK hosted edge and then in Dedicated once provisioned.
[08:14] Priya: I'll own the UK run and the baseline eval. I'll share the results in the benchmarking sheet and set up a short follow-up.
[08:22] Sophie: Sounds good. Also need the legal team to see indemnity and data residency clauses up front.
[08:29] Alex: We'll include standard indemnity language and the data residency addendum. We'll flag anything special for your legal.
[08:36] Marco: On the rollout: can you support canary/A-B between regions? We want to divert a small % to the UK endpoint first.
[08:44] Priya: Yes, smart routing supports traffic split by route, model, and region. You can define policies for latency floors or fallback to hosted.
[08:54] Karen: That is helpful. One more operational ask — how do we manage secrets and rotations if using BYOK?
[09:02] Priya: We integrate with external KMS and have an API for rotation. We'll send the runbook. There's a one-time handshake for key access.
[09:11] Alex: Let's quickly talk payment profiles: monthly versus annual commit — multi-year gets you better committed pricing and a predictable committed spend for Redwood to provision Dedicated capacity.
[09:24] Sophie: We prefer annual pre-pay if the discount is sizable. Could you show modeled cost for 12 vs 24 months?
[09:31] Alex: Yes, we'll include 12- and 24-month modeled scenarios in the quote with token-level math and the Dedicated base + burst +/- hosted fallback.
[09:40] Marco: Anything on SLAs? We need 99.9% uptime and rolling latency SLOs for the critical checkout route.
[09:48] Alex: We can offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers; latency SLOs are included as part of the service level review and can be contractual for Dedicated plus observability credits. We'll put that in the contract language.
[10:02] Karen: All right, let's discuss timeline and immediate blockers.
[10:07] Eli: Our networking team will need a list of egress IPs and peering details to start security reviews.
[10:12] Priya: We'll provide a networking pack with sample CloudFormation/IaC snippets and the egress ranges.
[10:18] Alex: Per earlier, next steps will be: updated quote by Mar 24, benchmarking run for UK by Mar 30, procurement confirmation by Apr 15. Anything else?
[10:29] Tanya: Can we get a short architecture workshop next week with our infra and Redwood SEs? 30–45 minutes to go over the VPC and key rotation flows.
[10:38] Alex: Yes, Priya — can you do that?
[10:41] Priya: Yep I'll schedule a 45-minute whiteboard on Tue or Wed next week. I'll invite Eli and Tanya.
[10:49] Sophie: One small ask: please include a clear line item for console/dashboards extra retention so finance can see the cost to keep logs 12 months vs 6 months.
[10:58] Alex: Will do. We'll make that explicit in the quote.
[11:03] Karen: That covers our open items from the product side. Anything else from Redwood?
[11:08] Jared: Just posted the onboarding playbook and the benchmarking spreadsheet in the thread (link: https://drive.example/prl-bench).
[11:14] Marco: Thanks.
[11:16] Alex: Okay wrapping — recap and owners. I'll send the quote and legal pack. Priya will run the UK benchmarks. Jared will push playbook. Sophie to confirm procurement timeline. Eli to provide egress/peering constraints.
[11:31] Sophie: We aim to have PO submitted by Apr 12 if everything looks good.
[11:35] Karen: Thanks all.
[11:37] Alex: Thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the artifacts.
